text: Employees must not accept any gift with a value exceeding EUR 50 from a current or prospective supplier.
Gifts and hospitality must be registered in the company's gift register within five business days of receipt.
This policy applies to all employees, contractors and temporary staff of the organisation.
A gift means any item, service or benefit of value offered without expectation of direct payment.
The purpose of this policy is to prevent gifts and hospitality from improperly influencing business decisions.
Any exception to the EUR 50 threshold requires prior written approval from the Compliance Officer.
This policy applies in all jurisdictions in which the company operates, subject to stricter local law.
Failure to comply with this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.
The UK Bribery Act 2010 imposes criminal liability on both individuals and organisations for bribery offences.
All employees must complete anti-bribery training annually as a condition of continued employment.
Consider whether the gift is offered in connection with a pending negotiation -- this is a common red flag.
Do not accept cash or cash-equivalent gifts under any circumstances, regardless of value.
For example, a branded pen worth EUR 5 received at a trade fair would not require registration.
